text: To understand why we built the system, we have to go back to the early days of coding agents, right?

text: So just like any other company, even at LinkedIn, we wanted to use the coding agents for our engineers and everyone to be really productive with the AI.

text: So what used to happen was the engineers used to do wipe code or try the agentic coding, but because the agents lacked context, they used to hallucinate and get stuck in between, or even more dangerous, they used to make up things which is not correct.

text: So the engineers had to prompt these agents
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So in early 2025, last year, so Anthropic released MCP and it quickly became the industry standard for building tools to the agents.

text: The second problem was context overload.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: As agents use more and more tools,
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Their context gets overloaded, which means every tool output, it takes up space in the context, which will eventually cause the agent to compact its, while it is working, compact its context, which causes it to lose some of the information.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Then it has to do all over again.

text: And the third problem was even if the agent was able to figure out all these details, it doesn't have a way to retain this information.

text: So how do we solve this problem?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we give these instructions right away, right?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we built a system, we invented a system in early 2025 called as Playbooks, where we not only provide the tools to the agents via MCP, we also allow the agents to access these instructions and prompts via MCP.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We call it Playbooks.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And playbook, it just appears just like any other regular tool.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And they have names and description on what it does.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the agent can decide to invoke that playbook just like any other regular tool.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And when the playbook is invoked, the instructions and the context within that playbook are returned as the tool output to the coding agent.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So that way the agents have both tools as well as instructions on how to use tools to set up or perform a task.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: For example, if the engineer goes and asks, how do I set up an Airflow DAG at LinkedIn, the agent will first decide, okay, so I have a playbook for creating that specific task, and it will use that first, uses that playbook to get the information, and then it calls the necessary, follows that instructions and calls the relevant tools to get the job done.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: This was really powerful.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Mainly because now anyone at LinkedIn can go ahead and create, set up a playbook and check it into a repository and make it available for everyone else at LinkedIn.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So as people started creating more playbooks, so we wanted, so this is one of two foundational principles we want everyone to follow when creating a playbook.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The first one is a playbook should be self-contained, which means it should do a very specific task.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Only, for example, if it is for setting up an Airflow DAG, it should be about the instruction and the construct should be about one specific task.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: This helps the agents pick the right playbook for the right task.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the second most important one is to break a big playbook into multiple smaller playbooks.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And reference those smaller playbooks from a bigger playbook.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: This is a really powerful principle because just like, so it has two main advantages, right?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So the first one is reusability.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So if you have a small self-contained playbooks, it can be used from multiple, referenced from multiple playbooks.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And if you, the another big advantage is progressive discovery of
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Context, which means the agent, only when it needs to read a smaller playbook, instead of reading the entire, all of the playbooks at once, it can progressively go and read the playbooks as it wants.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So this is the same concept as skills as well.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So playbooks are very similar to skills, but we developed this entire system around playbooks even before skills was a thing.

text: And Playbooks are a little bit more nuanced because it helps us seamlessly capture all of the organizational context and service via MCP without much of a setup.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And another cool thing about this Playbooks is the self-improving loop.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So you have engineers creating these playbooks and checking into the repository.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And one of the main problem with any knowledge base is it gets outdated.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The biggest problem is how do you keep the context fresh, right?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So great thing about agents is they can improvise.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So any outdated information or any discrepancy or any missing information
speaker: SPEAKER_00

speaker: SPEAKER_00
